subject: social_science

concepts.title: Estates System and Privileges of Old Regime France
concepts.definition: French society before 1789 was divided into three social classes where the nobility and clergy enjoyed inherited exemptions from state taxation.
concepts.key_idea: Feudal hierarchy exempted upper estates while burdening commoners with state taxes.
question_patterns: describe the structure of French society during the Old Regime
explain the privileges enjoyed by the first two estates in France
what was the composition of the Third Estate in 18th century France
how was French society organized prior to the revolution of 1789
identify the social groups exempted from paying taxes in pre-revolutionary France

solution_steps.explain: French society comprised the First Estate (clergy), Second Estate (nobility), and Third Estate (commoners including merchants, peasants, and workers).
First and Second Estates enjoyed tax exemptions by birth and extracted feudal dues, whereas the Third Estate alone paid direct and indirect state taxes.

concepts.title: Calculation of Tithe Tax
concepts.definition: The church in Old Regime France levied an agricultural tax called tithe, which equaled one-tenth of the total crop harvested by peasants.
concepts.key_idea: Tithe represents a direct 10 percent levy on agrarian yield collected by the clergy.
question_patterns: calculate the tithe payable on an agricultural produce of {produce} quintals
find the church tax tithe when the total harvest is {produce} kg
determine the tithe amount for a crop yield of {produce} bushels
what is the tithe tax on a grain produce of {produce} tonnes in pre-revolutionary France
compute the tax owed to the clergy given a total produce of {produce} units

solution_steps.explain: tithe is defined as one-tenth of the harvested agricultural produce

concepts.title: Causes and Mechanism of Subsistence Crisis
concepts.definition: An extreme economic situation in Old Regime France where rapid population growth outpaced grain production, leading to soaring bread prices and widespread starvation.
concepts.key_idea: Mismatch between population growth and food supply triggers escalating scarcity and mortality.
question_patterns: explain how a subsistence crisis occurred in France during the Old Regime
what factors led to frequent subsistence crises in 18th century France
describe the sequence of events resulting in a subsistence crisis
how did rapid population growth trigger food scarcity in pre-revolutionary France
analyse the impact of rising bread prices on the working class of Paris

solution_steps.explain: Population growth from 23 million to 28 million increased foodgrain demand faster than production could match.

solution_steps.action: examine price-wage gap and crop failure impact
solution_steps.explain: Bread prices escalated while fixed wages failed to keep pace, worsening into famine whenever bad weather ruined harvests.

concepts.title: Influence of Enlightenment Philosophers
concepts.definition: Ideas proposed by Locke, Rousseau, and Montesquieu challenged divine monarchical right, proposing social contracts and division of government powers.
concepts.key_idea: Enlightenment philosophy articulated equality, popular sovereignty, and separation of powers.
question_patterns: examine the role of philosophers in inspiring the French Revolution
what ideas were proposed by John Locke in Two Treatises of Government
how did Jean Jacques Rousseau contribute to revolutionary thinking in France
describe Montesquieu's theory on division of power in government
discuss how political ideas spread among the French public in salons and coffee houses

solution_steps.explain: Locke wrote Two Treatises of Government, Rousseau authored The Social Contract, and Montesquieu penned The Spirit of the Laws.
Locke refuted royal divine right, Rousseau proposed representative social contracts, and Montesquieu advocated legislative, executive, and judicial power division.

concepts.title: Convocation of Estates General and Voting Rights Conflict
concepts.definition: The assembly representing all three estates called on 5 May 1789, where dispute over voting by order versus individual voting led to Third Estate walkout.
concepts.key_idea: Refusal of individual voting rights sparked political rebellion by Third Estate representatives.
question_patterns: why was the meeting of the Estates General called on 5 May 1789
explain the disagreement over voting procedure in the Estates General
what led representatives of the Third Estate to walk out of the Estates General
describe the seating arrangement and representation in the Estates General of 1789
how did Rousseau's democratic principle influence the demands of the Third Estate

solution_steps.explain: Louis XVI summoned 300 clergy, 300 nobles, and 600 Third Estate delegates to approve new tax proposals.
Third Estate demanded one vote per member instead of one vote per estate; royal rejection prompted their protest walkout.

concepts.title: Tennis Court Oath and Outbreak of Revolution
concepts.definition: The Third Estate declared itself the National Assembly on 20 June 1789 at Versailles, swearing to draft a constitution limiting royal power.
concepts.key_idea: Self-declaration as National Assembly and Tennis Court Oath marked the formal shift away from absolutism.
question_patterns: what was the significance of the Tennis Court Oath in 1789
who led the Third Estate during the assembly at the indoor tennis court
explain the circumstances surrounding the storming of the Bastille on 14 July 1789
how did rumors of brigands trigger rural agrarian revolts across France
describe the measures taken by the National Assembly on 4 August 1789

solution_steps.explain: Led by Mirabeau and Sieyes, delegates pledged to remain assembled until drafting a constitution to constrain royal power.
Parisians stormed the Bastille on 14 July 1789, while rural panic sparked peasant attacks on chateaux, forcing abolition of feudalism on 4 August 1789.

concepts.title: Active Citizen Voting Threshold Computation
concepts.definition: Under the 1791 Constitution, voting rights were granted only to men above 25 who paid direct tax equal to at least three days of a worker's wage.
concepts.key_idea: Financial threshold for active citizenship required tax equivalent to three days of manual labor wages.
question_patterns: calculate the minimum tax required to become an active citizen if the daily wage is {daily_wage} livres
find the tax threshold for voting rights when a labourer earns {daily_wage} livres per day
determine the voting tax requirement for a worker earning {daily_wage} francs daily
what is the minimum direct tax needed for active citizenship given a daily wage of {daily_wage} livres
compute the tax payable to qualify as an active citizen with daily wage {daily_wage} livres

solution_steps.explain: active citizen status required direct tax equivalent to at least 3 days of a labourer's wage

concepts.title: Rights of Man and Political Symbolism
concepts.definition: The 1791 Constitution incorporated natural inalienable rights alongside visual political symbols to convey revolutionary values to an illiterate populace.
concepts.key_idea: Declaration enshrined natural rights while allegorical symbols communicated liberty, equality, and unity.
question_patterns: what were natural and inalienable rights according to the Declaration of 1791
explain the meaning of visual political symbols like the broken chain and Phrygian cap
describe the significance of the winged woman and the all-seeing eye in revolutionary art
how did the Declaration of Rights of Man define liberty and law
why were political symbols extensively used in revolutionary France

solution_steps.explain: Rights to life, speech, opinion, and equality before law were established as inherent human rights that state law must protect.
Broken chains represented liberation from servitude, red Phrygian cap symbolized freed slaves, and fasces denoted strength through unity.

concepts.title: Jacobin Club, Sans-Culottes, and Establishment of Republic
concepts.definition: Political radicalization led by Robespierre's Jacobins (sans-culottes) resulted in the storming of Tuileries, ending monarchy and creating the Republic in 1792.
concepts.key_idea: Radical lower-class mobilization replaced constitutional monarchy with a elected republic.
question_patterns: who were the Jacobins and who was their prominent leader
explain the term sans-culottes and their distinctive style of dress
how did France transition from constitutional monarchy to a republic in 1792
describe the events of 10 August 1792 at the Palace of Tuileries
what was the role of political clubs during the French revolutionary period

solution_steps.explain: Jacobins comprised small artisans and workers led by Robespierre, adopting striped long trousers to distinguish themselves from aristocrats.
Parisians stormed Tuileries on 10 August 1792, suspended royalty, and elected the Convention, which declared France a Republic on 21 September 1792.

concepts.title: Reign of Terror under Robespierre
concepts.definition: The period from 1793 to 1794 characterized by Robespierre's harsh policies of state control, price ceilings, rationing, and execution by guillotine.
concepts.key_idea: State control and violent suppression of perceived political enemies defined the Reign of Terror.
question_patterns: why is the period from 1793 to 1794 referred to as the Reign of Terror
describe the economic control measures implemented by Robespierre's government
what was the guillotine and how was it utilized during the Reign of Terror
how did Robespierre enforce socio-economic equality in daily French life
explain the circumstances that led to the downfall and execution of Robespierre

solution_steps.explain: Suspected political opponents were arrested, tried by revolutionary tribunals, and executed via the guillotine.
The state imposed maximum price and wage limits, rationed bread/meat, banned white flour, and renamed titles to Citoyen and Citoyenne.

concepts.title: Role and Demands of Women in the Revolution
concepts.definition: Women actively participated in revolution through political clubs like the Society of Revolutionary and Republican Women, demanding equal voting and civil rights.
concepts.key_idea: Women fought for civil and political rights, facing suppression under the Terror before securing suffrage in 1946.
question_patterns: describe the role played by women during the French Revolution
what were the main demands of women's political clubs in France
who was Olympe de Gouges and what was her contribution to women's rights
how did the revolutionary government modify laws concerning women's marriage and education
when did women in France finally win the right to vote

solution_steps.explain: Women formed around sixty political clubs and Olympe de Gouges authored the Declaration of the Rights of Woman and Citizen.

solution_steps.action: examine legal reforms and long-term suffrage outcome
solution_steps.explain: Early revolutionary laws mandated schooling for girls and legalized civil marriage contracts, though female political voting was only granted in 1946.

concepts.title: Triangular Slave Trade and Abolition in French Colonies
concepts.definition: A maritime commercial network connecting Europe, Africa, and Americas to supply plantation commodities, abolished by Convention in 1794 and permanently in 1848.
concepts.key_idea: Port prosperity relied on forced labor until colonial slavery was legally eradicated.
question_patterns: explain the operation of the triangular slave trade between Europe, Africa, and the Americas
which French port cities grew prosperous due to the flourishing slave trade
when was slavery first abolished in French colonies and who reintroduced it
why was the National Assembly hesitant to abolish slavery in the late 18th century
in which year was slavery permanently abolished in all French possessions

solution_steps.explain: French merchants bought African slaves from coastal chieftains and transported them to Caribbean plantations supplying tobacco, sugar, indigo, and coffee.
The Convention abolished colonial slavery in 1794, Napoleon reinstated it in 1804, and final complete abolition was achieved in 1848.
